newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian opposition says won't boycott elections.
newsitem.headline: Albanian opposition says won't boycott elections.

text.p: Two Albanian opposition parties said on Thursday they would take part in October 20 local elections, abondoning earlier threats of a boycott unless their demands were met.
"Our fight should be held at the voting centres," said Skender Gjinushi of the centre-left Social Democrats, which will run in alliance with the centre-right Democratic Alliance party.
"Our main achievement would be holding free and fair elections, though the situation until now is not so promising," said Democratic Alliance leader Neritan Ceka, who will run for mayor of Tirana.

Albania's nationwide local elections come barely five months after the country's third multi-party parliamentary elections on May 26 and June 2 were boycotted by most of the opposition which accused the Democrats of vote rigging.
President Sali Berisha of the ruling Democrats bowed to Western pressure and gave the opposition parties a bigger role in the current polls, but they said his concessions had not gone far enough.

Opposition parties also attacked a new law according to which members of local electoral commissions who boycott the polls while voting is still under way could be sentenced to up to three years in jail.
